input.question: Which league does Dave Carrick play in?

documents.text: As the sun dipped below the horizon on a crisp autumn evening in 1971, Dave Carrick laced up his skates and stepped onto the ice at the Lafayette College rink. The same hands that had once dribbled a basketball with precision now gripped a hockey stick, his fingers instinctively finding the familiar contours. It was a peculiar sight, one that raised more than a few eyebrows among the Lafayette faithful. After all, Dave was a basketball legend, a shooting guard who had electrified the college hoops scene with his silky smooth jump shot and lightning-quick drives to the rim. But Dave had a secret: he was a hockey player at heart. Growing up in the frozen tundras of upstate New York, he had spent countless hours on the outdoor rinks, his parents bundling him up in layers of wool and down to brave the biting winds. The speed, the skill, the physicality – it all came so naturally to him. And yet, he had never pursued it seriously, opting instead to follow the basketball dream to Lafayette. Now, as he glided effortlessly across the ice, his stickhandling skills rusty but still impressive, Dave felt an itch he couldn't scratch. The thrill of competition, the rush of adrenaline as he battled for puck possession – it was all so intoxicating. He began to wonder: what if? What if he had chosen hockey instead of hoops? Would he be playing in the National Hockey League right now, instead of suiting up for the Lafayette Leopards? The thought lingered, a tantalizing whisper in the back of his mind, as Dave finished his impromptu skate and headed back to the locker room. Little did he know, fate was about to intervene, and the answer to that what-if would soon become a reality.
